claims.text: Atlassian Marketplace enterprise multi-instance pricing can charge based on unique users across instances.
claims.source_title: Atlassian Marketplace apps: Pricing, payment, and billing
claims.research_note: Official marketplace documentation describes unique-user multi-instance charging.

claims.text: Slack bills paid workspaces for active members and excludes inactive or deactivated members under its Fair Billing Policy.
claims.research_note: Official billing policy states the active-member basis.

claims.text: monday.com prices its work-management plans in seat buckets rather than exact individual seats.
claims.research_note: Official support documentation describes minimum and ascending seat buckets.

claims.text: Linear offers a free plan and public paid per-user plans.
claims.research_note: Official pricing page publishes free and per-user paid tiers.

claims.text: BetterCloud states that pricing reflects license count, connected apps, selected modules, and add-ons.
claims.research_note: Official pricing FAQ directly lists these pricing dimensions.

claims.text: FOCUS 1.4 defines a normalized technology billing-data specification for allocation, reporting, and analysis.
claims.research_note: The official specification defines normalized billing data requirements.

claims.text: FinOps unit economics connects technology cost with measurable business value and unit outcomes.
claims.research_note: Official framework describes value-to-cost and AI value KPIs.

claims.text: A hybrid connected-application and unique-protected-user metric best matches Concord's integration cost and customer coverage value.
claims.research_note: Application count approximates connector cost while unique protected users avoids duplicate charging across systems.

claims.text: AppOmni positions its platform around continuous SaaS and AI posture, identity, privilege, threat detection, and governance.
claims.research_note: Official vendor page documents current positioning; performance was not independently validated.

claims.text: Noma positions its platform around AI discovery, governance, testing, runtime protection, and response.
claims.research_note: Official vendor page documents product scope; cross-derivative retrieval proof was not found.

claims.text: Zenity positions its platform around agent configuration, permissions, runtime enforcement, and response across SaaS and cloud agents.
claims.source_title: AI Agent Security and Governance Platform
claims.research_note: Official vendor page supports agent-security overlap.

claims.text: Grip Security describes an AI identity graph mapping users, agents, applications, permissions, and data.
claims.research_note: Official vendor article supports the emerging-threat pathway.

claims.text: Token Security positions its platform around non-human identity discovery, lifecycle governance, and automated remediation for AI agents.
claims.source_title: Token Security AI Agent and NHI Security Platform
claims.research_note: Official vendor page supports identity and remediation adjacency.

claims.text: Saviynt Zuma positions itself as an AI identity control plane that discovers agents, authorizes actions, and governs lifecycle.
claims.research_note: Official product page supports the adjacent-platform classification.

claims.text: ARMO argues for independent two-plane verification in enterprise agent governance.
claims.source_title: AI Agent Governance: From Policy Framework to Runtime
claims.research_note: Official vendor thought leadership is a directional signal, not proof of shipped capability.

claims.text: ElixirData describes runtime policy gates and decision traces for governed AI agents.
claims.source_title: Runtime Policy Enforcement for AI Agents
claims.research_note: Public vendor article provides a weak product-direction signal; production maturity is unknown.

search_scope.result: No authorized Crunchbase capability was present.

claims.text: No publicly documented vendor was verified as offering Concord's complete source-change, cross-derivative repair, destination read-back, affected-identity retrieval proof, and evidence workflow.
claims.research_note: Reviewed functional, adjacent, and emerging vendors show substantial partial overlap but not the complete documented loop. This does not prove no private capability exists.

claims.text: Zylo publicly packages its platform as Core, Premium, and Enterprise and asks customers to request a quote rather than publishing numeric list prices.
claims.source_title: Zylo Pricing: Enterprise SaaS Management Plans
claims.research_note: The official pricing page names the three packages and uses request-a-quote calls to action.

claims.text: CloudEagle's official pricing page presents separate AI Governance, SaaS Security, Identity Governance, SaaS Management, and Procurement modules, alongside demo and free-trial entry points.
claims.research_note: The official pricing page lists modular packages and entry calls to action; no independent validation of claimed savings was performed.

claims.text: Lumos states that its custom enterprise pricing is tied to identity and application count.
claims.source_title: The Top 5 Saviynt Competitors for Identity Governance in 2026
claims.research_note: The structural pricing description appears on Lumos's own comparison content and was not independently verified from a customer contract.

claims.text: Numeric list prices were not publicly documented in the reviewed official pricing or product pages for Torii, Zluri, AppOmni, and Lumos.
claims.research_note: Official pages exposed packages, demos, product scope, or custom-quote language but did not provide sufficient public numeric list prices for a reliable benchmark.
